subtitle: Lesson 5 · Azure Identity & Access Security

eyebrow: Every policy is four decisions, not one

steps.label: Assignments
steps.sub: which users/groups and cloud apps — including workload identities, assigned separately

steps.label: Conditions
steps.sub: sign-in risk, device platform, named locations, client app type

steps.label: Grant + session controls
steps.sub: what's required to get in (MFA, compliant device) and what applies after (sign-in frequency)

code:
# Policy A: this user -> require MFA
# Policy B: this user -> require compliant device
#
# Both match the sign-in, so BOTH grant controls apply:
# the user needs MFA AND a compliant device.
#
# Entra ID never picks "the best matching policy" --
# every matching policy's grant controls stack.
caption: Design each new policy assuming it will combine with everything already in the tenant.

eyebrow: The failure mode that locks out the whole tenant

steps.label: Cloud-only Global Administrator account
steps.sub: not synced from on-prem AD, so an on-prem outage can't take it down too

steps.label: Credential stored outside the tenant
steps.sub: long, randomly generated, kept in a sealed physical or offline process

steps.label: Explicitly excluded from every CA policy
steps.sub: if it's not excluded, a misfiring policy can lock out your only way back in

code:
# New Conditional Access policy workflow:
#
# 1. Build policy, set state = Report-only
# 2. Let it run against real sign-ins
# 3. Review Sign-in logs -> Conditional Access tab
#    (success / failure / not-applicable per policy)
# 4. Use the "What If" tool for one simulated sign-in
# 5. Only then: switch state to On
caption: Report-only mode logs what would have happened without blocking anyone.
